streamlabs.connected.description: Runs when Cuebot connects to Streamlabs. Handy for a quick "all good" message or to switch something on.

streamlabs.disconnected.description: Runs when Cuebot loses or ends its connection to Streamlabs. Handy to warn yourself that alerts have stopped.

streamlabs.donation.description: Runs when someone donates through Streamlabs. Great for a thank-you message or an alert.

fields.minAmount: The smallest amount that runs this. Example: 5 ignores anything under 5. Leave 0 to run for any amount. Amounts are not converted between currencies.
fields.maxAmount: The biggest amount that runs this. Leave 0 for no upper limit.
fields.currency: Only run for these currencies. Type the short codes with commas, like "USD, EUR". Leave empty for every currency.
fields.includeTests: Tick to also run for test events (made with a "send test" button). Untick to run only for real ones.
fields.includeBackfill: Tick to also run for donations Cuebot fetched after the connection came back (they happened while it was down). Needs your Streamlabs app connected.

variables.amount: The amount as a number, like 5 or 12.5
variables.donationId: The number Streamlabs gave this donation
variables.isTest: True when this is a test event, not a real one
variables.isBackfill: True when Cuebot fetched this donation after a reconnect instead of hearing it live
variables.emotes: Emote data Streamlabs sent with the message, if any

streamelements.streamOnline.description: Runs when StreamElements sees your stream go live on any platform it watches. Also sets the global ~seIsLive~ to true.

streamelements.sessionUpdated.description: Runs when a StreamElements session value changes, like the latest follower or the tip goal. The values are also kept in globals like ~se.tipSession.amount~.

fields.key: Only run for these session keys, like "tip-goal, follower-latest". Leave empty for every change.

variables.key: Which session value changed, like tip-session
variables.variable: The start of its global names, like se.tipSession
variables.name: A name that came with it (for example the latest follower)
variables.amount: An amount that came with it
variables.count: A count that came with it

streamelements.sessionReset.description: Runs when your StreamElements session starts over (by hand or on the automatic reset). The se.* globals are refilled.

streamelements.overlayUpdated.description: Runs when one of your StreamElements overlays is changed and saved. Handy to know it is time to import it into Cuebot again.

variables.dataJson: Everything that came with it, as JSON text
variables.data.<name>: One detail that came with it, by name

variables.slAlertsPaused: True when the alert queue is paused

streamlabs.createAlert.description: Shows your own alert in the Streamlabs alert box, styled like one of its alert types. Streamlabs asks apps to send at most 2 a minute, so Cuebot waits when you send more. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

fields.type: Which alert style to borrow: donation, follow, subscription or host.
fields.message: The main text. Put words in *stars* to highlight them, like *%user%* says hi.
fields.userMessage: Optional second line under the main text.
fields.image: Optional link to an image or GIF. Empty uses the alert type's own.
fields.sound: Optional link to a sound. Empty uses the alert type's own.
fields.duration: How long it shows, in milliseconds (5000 = 5 seconds). 0 uses the default.
fields.color: Optional colour of the highlighted words, like #32C3A6.

streamlabs.sendTestAlert.description: Asks Streamlabs to play one of its own test alerts in your alert box. Unlike "Send test event" on the Donations page, this shows on stream. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

streamlabs.setAlertProfile.description: Switches your Streamlabs alert profile, for example to a calmer set while Just Chatting. Pair it with a scene change. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

fields.profile: The profile name as Streamlabs shows it (capitals do not matter).

variables.slAlertProfileId: The id of the profile switched to

streamlabs.spinWheel.description: Spins your Streamlabs spin-the-wheel widget. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

streamlabs.emptyJar.description: Empties your Streamlabs tip jar widget. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

streamlabs.rollCredits.description: Rolls your Streamlabs end credits. Streamlabs only rolls them while you are live; otherwise the step fails with a message saying so. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

streamlabs.mediaShare.description: Controls Streamlabs media share: play, pause, skip, volume, and turning requests, autoplay, auto-show or moderation on or off. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

fields.volume: For the volume actions only: a level from 0 to 100. Leave empty to change by Streamlabs' own step.

streamlabs.getDonations.description: Gets your latest Streamlabs donations, newest first. Handy for a "last donation" command or credits. Needs your own Streamlabs app connected (Donations → Streamlabs → Connect with Streamlabs).

fields.amount: How many points to give. Use a minus sign, like -50, to take points away.

streamelements.getPointsLeaderboard.description: Looks up your top viewers by StreamElements loyalty points. Handy to read out a top list in chat.

fields.count: How many people to fetch, starting from the top. 5 gets the top five.
fields.board: Which list: current points, all-time points (everything they ever earned) or watch time.

variables.sePointsLeader0User: The name of number 1 (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)
variables.sePointsLeader0Total: Their points (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamelements.getTips.description: Looks up your most recent StreamElements tips. Handy to show or read out the latest supporters.

fields.count: How many of the latest tips to fetch. 5 gets the five newest.

variables.seTip0User: Who sent the newest tip (use 1, 2, 3... for older ones)
variables.seTip0Amount: How much it was (use 1, 2, 3... for older ones)

streamelements.getTipLeaderboard.description: Looks up the people who tipped you the most on StreamElements. Handy for a thank-you list.

fields.count: How many people to fetch, starting from the top. 5 gets the top five.
fields.period: Which time span to count: all time, this month, this week or this stream.

variables.seTipLeader0User: The name of number 1 (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)
variables.seTipLeader0Total: How much they tipped in total (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamelements.botSay.description: Sends a chat message as the StreamElements bot. The bot must be in your chat (dashboard → Chatbot).

fields.message: What the bot should say, like "Thanks for the tip, %user%!"

streamelements.botMute.description: Mutes the StreamElements bot (it stops talking in chat) or unmutes it.

fields.state: Mute to silence the bot, Unmute to let it talk again.

streamelements.getBotStatus.description: Checks whether the StreamElements bot is in your chat, muted or a moderator.

variables.seBotJoined: True when it is in your chat
variables.seBotMod: True when it is a moderator

streamelements.getCounter.description: Reads a StreamElements chatbot counter, like a death counter.

fields.counter: The counter's name as in StreamElements, like "deaths".

streamelements.setTimer.description: Turns a StreamElements chatbot timer on or off, for example only during a certain game.

fields.timer: The timer's name as in StreamElements, like "Discord".
fields.state: On, Off, or Toggle to flip it.

variables.seTimerEnabled: True when the timer is on now

streamelements.setCommand.description: Turns a StreamElements chatbot command on or off.

fields.state: On, Off, or Toggle to flip it.

variables.seCommandEnabled: True when the command is on now

streamelements.overlayAction.description: Controls your StreamElements overlays: pause or play the alert queue, mute or unmute them, or reload them.

fields.action: pause holds alerts, play lets them run again, mute/unmute switch their sound, reload refreshes every overlay.

streamelements.setSessionValue.description: Changes one StreamElements session value, like the tip goal. Handy to set a goal from an action.

fields.key: The session key, like "tip-goal" or "follower-goal". The keys are listed in StreamElements' session data reference.
fields.field: Which part of it, like "amount" or "count".

streamelements.resetSession.description: Starts a new StreamElements session: session counts and amounts go back to 0, like the dashboard's reset button.

streamelements.replayLatest.description: Asks StreamElements to send your newest real event of a kind again (like the dashboard's replay). Handy to test alerts end to end.

fields.type: Which kind of event to replay, like a tip.

variables.seReplayedId: The replayed event's id (empty when there was none)

streamelements.getUserRank.description: Looks up a viewer's place on your StreamElements points list.

fields.user: The viewer's login name. The default %userName% means the person who ran the action. Make sure it is their name on the streaming site.

streamelements.resetUserPoints.description: Sets a viewer's StreamElements points back to 0.

fields.user: The viewer's login name. The default %userName% means the person who ran the action. Make sure it is their name on the streaming site.

streamelements.bulkPoints.description: Gives (or sets) the same StreamElements points for many viewers at once, like "everyone in chat gets 50".

fields.users: The viewers' names, separated by commas or spaces, like "anna, ben, cleo".
fields.amount: How many points. Use a minus number with Add to take some away.
fields.mode: Add adds to what they have; Set replaces it.

streamelements.resetPoints.description: Resets everyone's StreamElements points. Careful: this cannot be undone.

fields.context: current resets the points people have now; alltime resets the all-time list.

streamelements.getCheerLeaderboard.description: Looks up who cheered the most bits, as StreamElements counted them.

fields.count: How many people to fetch. 5 gets five.
fields.period: Which time span: all time, this month, this week or this stream.

variables.seCheerLeader0User: Number 1's name (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamelements.createTip.description: Adds a tip to your StreamElements tip list, for example one paid somewhere else, so goals and leaderboards count it. It does not take money.

fields.currency: The 3-letter currency code, like USD or EUR.

streamelements.getPendingTips.description: Looks up StreamElements tips waiting for a moderator to approve them.

variables.seTip0User: Who sent the first (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamelements.getStoreItem.description: Looks up an item in your StreamElements loyalty store.

fields.item: The item's name as in your store, like "Hydrate!".

variables.seItemEnabled: True when it can be bought
variables.seItemStock: How many are left (-1 for no limit)

streamelements.setStoreItem.description: Changes an item in your StreamElements loyalty store: turn it on or off, change its price or how many are left.

fields.item: The item's name as in your store, like "Hydrate!".
fields.state: Keep leaves it as it is; On, Off or Toggle switches it.
fields.cost: The new price in points. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.stock: How many are left. Leave empty to keep it.

variables.seItemEnabled: True when it can be bought now

streamelements.completeRedemption.description: Marks a StreamElements store redemption as done.

fields.redemptionId: The redemption's id. %redemptionId% is the one that started this action.

streamelements.refundRedemption.description: Cancels a StreamElements store redemption and gives the viewer their points back.

fields.redemptionId: The redemption's id. %redemptionId% is the one that started this action.

streamelements.getPendingRedemptions.description: Looks up StreamElements store redemptions that are not done yet.

fields.count: How many redemptions to fetch. 5 gets five.

variables.seRedemption0Item: The first one's item (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamelements.createContest.description: Creates a StreamElements contest where viewers bet points on an answer. Start it with Run contest.

fields.title: The question, like "Will I beat the boss?".
fields.options: The answers, separated by commas, like "Yes, No".
fields.minutes: How many minutes betting stays open.

streamelements.contestAction.description: Starts, closes, refunds or picks the winner of a StreamElements contest.

fields.action: start opens betting, close stops it, winner pays out, refund gives every bet back.
fields.winner: For winner: the winning answer's name or number, like "Yes" or 1.
fields.contestId: Leave empty for the current contest.

streamelements.getContest.description: Looks up the current StreamElements contest.

variables.seContestOption0Title: The first answer (use 1, 2... for the next)

streamelements.giveawayAction.description: Starts, closes, draws a winner for, completes, reopens or refunds a StreamElements giveaway.

fields.action: What to do with the giveaway.
fields.giveawayId: Leave empty for the current giveaway.

streamelements.getGiveaway.description: Looks up the current StreamElements giveaway.

streamelements.songPlayer.description: Plays or pauses StreamElements song requests.

streamelements.getSong.description: Looks up the StreamElements song request playing now, or the next one.

fields.which: playing for the song now, next for the one after it.

streamelements.addSong.description: Adds a song to your StreamElements song request queue.

fields.video: A YouTube link, video id or search words. %rawInput% is what the viewer typed after the command.

streamelements.removeSong.description: Removes a song from your StreamElements song request queue.

streamelements.getSongQueue.description: Looks up the songs waiting in your StreamElements song request queue.

fields.count: How many songs to fetch. 5 gets five.

variables.seQueue0Title: The first one's title (use 1, 2, 3... for the next ones)

streamloots.sendTestEvent.description: Makes a pretend StreamLoots alert so you can try your actions without waiting for a real one.

fields.kind: Which pretend alert to make: a purchase, a gift to one person, a gift to the community, or a card played.

crowdcontrol.getSession.description: Checks the current Crowd Control play session and saves the answer in variables. Handy to show what game is running.

variables.ccConnected: True if Cuebot is connected to Crowd Control
variables.ccSessionActive: True if a play session is running
variables.ccTimedEffectCount: How many lasting effects are running
variables.ccTimedEffects: The names of those effects, joined with commas

crowdcontrol.sendTestEvent.description: Makes a pretend Crowd Control event so you can try your actions without a real viewer.

fields.kind: Which pretend event to make, like effectSuccess for a working effect or coinExchange for coins added.

kofi.getGoal.description: Reads the Ko-fi goal Cuebot keeps, so you can say it in chat or show it.

kofi.setGoal.description: Changes the Ko-fi goal. Handy for a chat command that sets a new target. Empty boxes keep what is there.

fields.title: The goal's new name. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.target: The new target, like 200. 0 turns the goal off. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.startAmount: What your Ko-fi goal already showed before Cuebot counted. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.currency: Only payments in this currency count, like USD. Leave empty to keep it.

kofi.addToGoal.description: Adds an amount to the Ko-fi goal by hand, like money that came in another way. A negative number takes it away.

fields.amount: How much to add, like 5. Use -5 to take 5 away.

kofi.resetGoal.description: Starts the Ko-fi goal again from its start amount.

fields.clearStart: Tick to set the start amount to 0 too.

kofi.addCommission.description: Adds a commission to the list by hand. Ko-fi commissions are added for you.

fields.name: Who it is for.
fields.amount: What they paid. Leave 0 if you like.
fields.currency: The currency code, like USD.

variables.commissionsOpen: How many commissions are open now

kofi.completeCommission.description: Marks a commission done, so it leaves the open list and overlays.

fields.which: Leave empty for the oldest open one. Or type its number in the list (1 is the oldest), or its id.

variables.commissionFound: False when there was no such open commission

kofi.getCommissions.description: Reads the open commissions, oldest first. Handy for a !queue chat command.

variables.commissionsText: The list as one line, like "1. Ana: a cat portrait; 2. Ben: a logo"
variables.commission0.name: The oldest one's name (commission1... for the next)

kofi.clearCommissions.description: Removes done commissions from the list.

fields.all: Tick to remove open ones too (empties the list).

patreon.getPatron.description: Checks whether a viewer is your Patreon patron, for chat perks and greetings. Works for patrons who linked Twitch or YouTube on Patreon.

fields.platform: Which platform the viewer is on: twitch, youtube or discord. %platform% is the chatter's.
fields.userId: The viewer's user id. %userId% is the chatter's.
fields.userName: The viewer's name. Used for Twitch when the patron linked Twitch by name only.

variables.isPatron: True if the viewer is an active patron
variables.isPayingPatron: True if they pay now (not a free trial or a gift)

patreon.getCampaign.description: Reads your Patreon campaign's totals, like how many patrons pay and how much a month, to say in chat or show.

variables.patreonPatronCount: How many patrons the campaign has
variables.patreonPaidCount: How many paying patrons Cuebot knows
variables.patreonMonthly: The paying patrons' pledges per month added up

patreon.syncMembers.description: Reads your Patreon member list now (Cuebot also does it every 6 hours). Needs the Patreon API connected on the Webhooks page.

variables.patreonPatronCount: How many patrons the campaign has
variables.patreonPaidCount: How many paying patrons Cuebot knows
variables.patreonMonthly: The paying patrons' pledges per month added up

fourthwall.createPromo.description: Makes a new discount code in your Fourthwall shop, for "first 10 chatters get 20% off", raid rewards or channel point redeems. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.code: The code. Leave empty for a random one like STREAM7K2QXP.
fields.kind: Percent off, Amount off (in the currency below) or Free shipping.
fields.value: The percent, or the amount off.
fields.currency: The currency for Amount off, like USD.
fields.maxUses: How many times it can be used in total. 0 = no limit.
fields.oncePerCustomer: Tick so each customer can use it once.

variables.fw.promotionId: Its id (End promo code can use it)
variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.endPromo.description: Ends a Fourthwall discount code (or makes it live again). Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.code: The code, like STREAM20, or the promotion id. %fw.code% is the one Create promo code made.
fields.live: Tick to make the code live again instead of ending it.

variables.fw.usageCount: How many times it was used
variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.setAvailability.description: Shows or hides a Fourthwall product or collection, for a limited drop while you are live. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.id: The product's id, or the collection's id or slug (from its web address).
fields.available: Tick to show it, untick to hide it again.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.setStreaming.description: Tells Fourthwall your shop is streaming on Twitch (or that the stream ended). Viewers can only buy stream gifts while it is. Cuebot can also do this by itself (Webhooks page). Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.online: Tick for streaming now, untick for ended.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.getMembers.description: Reads how many Fourthwall members you have, in total and per tier, and can check whether an email belongs to a member. Counts come from webhooks and, with the Fourthwall API connected, the member list.

fields.email: Optional. An email to check, for example from a form or a command. Needs the API's member list.

variables.fourthwallTiers: Each tier with its member count, like "Gold (3), Silver (10)"
variables.fourthwallMembers.<tier>: The member count of one tier, like %fourthwallMembers.Gold%
variables.isFourthwallMember: True when the email belongs to an active member
variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.getTotals.description: Reads your Fourthwall sales since today, the last 24 hours, this stream or this month: purchases (not samples, claimed gifts or cancelled orders) and completed donations. Good for merch goals that survive a restart. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.period: Since when: Today, Last 24 hours, This stream (the hours below) or This month.
fields.hours: For This stream: how many hours back.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.createPost.description: Posts to your Fourthwall members, for example "I'm live!" when the stream starts. With a video link it is a video post. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.title: The post's title (at least 3 characters).
fields.videoUrl: Optional. A YouTube or Twitch link to embed.
fields.access: Who can see it: MembersOnly, Public or FreeAndPaidMembers.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.getThankYous.description: Lists supporters still waiting for a Fourthwall thank-you, to show or read out on stream. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

variables.fourthwallThankYouCount: How many are waiting (up to the maximum)
variables.thankYou0.id: The first one's id, for Send thank-you video (use 1, 2... for the next ones)
variables.thankYou0.name: The first one's name
variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.sendThankYou.description: Sends a video or picture as the thank-you to a Fourthwall supporter, for example an OBS replay you just saved. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.contributionId: Which supporter: the id from Get thank-yous waiting.
fields.file: The video or picture file on this PC.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.createGiveawayLinks.description: Makes Fourthwall giveaway links for a product: each link lets one person claim it for free. Send one to a winner by whisper or DM. Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

variables.fw.giveawayLink0: The first link (use 1, 2... for the next ones)
variables.fw.giveawayPackageId: The id of this batch of links
variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.refreshProducts.description: Reads your Fourthwall products again for the Products widget (Cuebot also does it after a product change and every 30 minutes). Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

fourthwall.catchUp.description: Asks Fourthwall which events it sent and runs those that never reached Cuebot (relay down, wrong secret). Cuebot also does this every few minutes (Webhooks page). Needs the Fourthwall API connected on the Webhooks page.

variables.fourthwallResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.getSales.description: Reads this stream's Shopify merch counter (paid orders minus cancellations and refunds) and goal, for a !merch command. No API needed.

variables.shopifyTopProduct: The product sold most this stream
variables.shopifySalesProductsText: Every product sold this stream, like "3 x Sticker pack, 1 x Hoodie"
variables.shopifyGoalReached: True when the target is reached
variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.resetSales.description: Starts the Shopify merch counter and goal again from zero (Cuebot also does it when a stream goes live, if that is ticked on the Webhooks page).

variables.shopifyTopProduct: The product sold most this stream
variables.shopifySalesProductsText: Every product sold this stream, like "3 x Sticker pack, 1 x Hoodie"
variables.shopifyGoalReached: True when the target is reached
variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.setGoal.description: Changes the Shopify merch goal. Empty boxes keep what is there.

fields.title: The goal's new name. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.target: The new target (items or money). 0 turns the goal off. Leave empty to keep it.
fields.measure: Count items sold or the money taken. Keep leaves it as it is.

variables.shopifyTopProduct: The product sold most this stream
variables.shopifySalesProductsText: Every product sold this stream, like "3 x Sticker pack, 1 x Hoodie"
variables.shopifyGoalReached: True when the target is reached
variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.getTotals.description: Reads your Shopify sales from Shopify itself (paid orders, not cancelled or test ones). Needs the Shopify API connected on the Webhooks page.

fields.since: This stream (since the merch counter started), today, or the last hours below.
fields.hours: How many hours back, for "The last hours below".

variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.getProducts.description: Lists your Shopify products (from the last refresh through the Shopify API), for a "what merch is there" command.

fields.search: Only products whose name contains this. Leave empty for all.

variables.shopifyProductsText: Names and prices joined with semicolons
variables.product0.name: The first product's name (product1.name for the second, and so on)
variables.product0.url: Its page in your online store
variables.product0.soldOut: True when it is sold out
variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.refreshProducts.description: Reads your Shopify products again for the Products widget and Get Shopify products. Needs the Shopify API connected.

variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed

shopify.catchUp.description: Asks Shopify for recently paid orders and runs Order Paid for those that never reached Cuebot (marked isReplay). Needs the Shopify API connected.

variables.shopifyResult: What happened, or why it failed
